skill.name: Outside Contain
skill.goal: Maintain outside leverage and force outside runs back toward defensive pursuit.

issue.name: Gives up the outside edge
issue.observableBehavior: Crashes inside against sweep action and allows the ball carrier outside.

diagnosticQuestions.text: Does the athlete understand force responsibility?
What does the athlete appear to watch first?
Is contact permitted in the next practice?

possibleCauses.name: Eye discipline
possibleCauses.explanation: The athlete may be following the ball before securing outside leverage.

possibleCauses.name: Force-responsibility understanding
possibleCauses.explanation: The athlete may not fully understand the responsibility to protect the edge and force the runner inside.

possibleCauses.name: Leverage and footwork
possibleCauses.explanation: The athlete may be stepping inside before the runner commits.

successCriteria.label: Forces the runner toward inside pursuit

drills.title: Mirror Shuffle
drills.equipment: Five-yard safe, flat space and one partner
instructions: The partner moves laterally at a controlled pace.
Shuffle while keeping outside leverage and shoulders square.
coachingPoints: Stop if the surface is unsafe or pain occurs.

drills.title: Force and Fold Recognition
instructions: Align the athlete as the force player.
Coach presents inside or outside movement.
Athlete identifies the outside threat and maintains leverage.
Begin at walk-through pace and progress only under coach control.
coachingPoints: Contact cannot be added automatically by the system.

lesson.title: Protect the Edge First
cues: Know your responsibility before the snap.
Stay square as long as possible.
Do not chase the ball before protecting the edge.

questions.text: What is the force player's first responsibility against an outside run?
questions.explanation: The force player protects the edge and directs the runner back toward inside pursuit.

questions.text: Which body position best supports outside contain?
options: Cross the feet toward the ball
questions.explanation: Staying square with outside leverage keeps the athlete ready to react without surrendering the edge.

questions.text: Where should the runner be directed?
questions.explanation: The defense is built to rally from the inside, so the force player directs the runner toward pursuit.

questions.text: When should the force player attack inside?
options: Only after protecting the edge and confirming the read
questions.explanation: Protect the edge first, then react after the runner and blocking path declare.

questions.text: What should stay free when setting the edge?
questions.explanation: Keeping the outside shoulder free helps prevent the runner from reaching the edge.
